f.title: Monitor safety of pharmaceutical preparations during the designated surveillance period
f.statement: The pharmaceutical dealer holding a permit for pharmaceutical preparations shall monitor the safety of the preparations within the period designated under Article 45(1) of the Act, which is based on the effective period shown on the Drug Permit. The surveillance covers: preparing a pharmacovigilance plan (Article 5) and reporting under Article 6; collecting new drug safety data and submitting reports under Articles 8 and 9; and preparing, implementing and reporting on the risk assessment and control plan for drugs of specific types or compositions (Article 10).
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Pharmaceutical preparations under a safety surveillance period set under PAA Article 45(1). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16). Under Article 4, Chinese medicines that are new drugs (Article 7 of the Act) or drugs announced or approved under Article 10(1) are also covered.
f.processes: Safety governance; Signal detection; Risk management & minimisation

rows.deadline: Within the surveillance period (based on the effective period shown on the Drug Permit, Article 2)
rows.quote:
The pharmaceutical dealer holding a permit for pharmaceutical preparations (hereinafter referred to as the pharmaceutical dealer) shall monitor the safety of the pharmaceutical preparations within the periods specified in the preceding article.
The surveillance of pharmaceutical safety in the preceding paragraph shall cover the following:
1. The preparation of a pharmacovigilance plan indicated in Article 5 and reporting indicated in Article 6.
2. Collection of new drug safety data and submission of reports indicated in Articles 8 and 9.
3. The preparation of the risk assessment and control plan consisting of drugs of specific types or compositions, its implementation, and submission of the reports indicated in Article 10.
rows.review_note: Review: applicability adds the Article 4 extension to Chinese medicines and the 1 January 2023 effective date (Article 16); otherwise no change. Double-check: quote proves the monitoring duty and its three components; the link of the period to the Drug Permit effective period comes from Article 2 and is not quoted; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Prepare a pharmacovigilance plan with the six required elements
f.statement: The pharmacovigilance plan prepared by the pharmaceutical dealer shall cover: (1) planning, operating and managing the surveillance procedure; (2) sources of pharmacovigilance information and method of collection; (3) evaluation and analysis of that information; (4) risk management for drugs with safety concerns; (5) responsibilities and functions of internal staff; (6) planning and implementing pharmacovigilance training programs.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Drugs under safety surveillance (Article 3). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.processes: Safety governance; Training & competency; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote:
The Pharmacovigilance Plan prepared by the pharmaceutical dealer shall cover the following:
1. Planning, operating, and managing the surveillance procedure.
2. Source of pharmacovigilance information and method of collection.
3. Evaluation and analysis of the information contained in the preceding sub-paragraph.
4. Risk management for drugs with safety concerns.
5. Responsibilities and functions of internal staff.
6. Planning and implementing pharmacovigilance training programs.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves all six plan elements, actor and modal; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Report safety findings online within 3 days of awareness
f.statement: The pharmaceutical dealer shall report through the online system established by the central competent health authority within three days from the day of awareness when: (1) unexpected serious adverse drug reactions occur, or serious adverse drug reactions occur at a frequency exceeding expectations; (2) new or altered contraindications or use restrictions need to be evaluated; (3) the drug is suspended or withdrawn from the market due to adverse reactions in an A10 country (Germany, US, UK, France, Japan, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Belgium, Sweden); (4) it is determined that a suspension or withdrawal due to adverse reactions in another country should be reported. 'Serious adverse drug reactions' in situation (1) are those defined in Article 4 of the Regulations for Reporting Severe Adverse Reactions of Medicaments.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Drugs under safety surveillance. Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.processes: Submission operations; Signal management; Reporting policy

rows.deadline: Within 3 days from the day of awareness of the situation
rows.quote:
the pharmaceutical dealer shall report it through the online system established by the central competent health authority within three days from the day of awareness of the situation:
1. Unexpected serious adverse drug reactions or serious adverse drug reactions occurs at a frequency that exceeds expectations.
2. It is required to evaluate new or altered contraindications or restricting use.
3. The drug is suspended or withdrawn from the market due to adverse reactions in A10 countries, which include Germany, US, UK, France, Japan, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Belgium, and Sweden.
4. It is determined that it should be reported when a drug is suspended or withdrawn from the market due to adverse reactions in countries other than those in the preceding subparagraph.
Serious adverse drug reactions indicated in Subparagraph 1 of the preceding paragraph refer to those indicated in Article 4 of the Regulations for Reporting Severe Adverse Reactions of Medicaments.
rows.review_note: Review: quote was cut before Article 6(2). Re-cut to start at "the pharmaceutical dealer shall report" to stay within 1000 characters, and extended to include Article 6(2), the definition reference for serious ADRs, which is now also in the statement. Note that the translation cites Article 4 of the serious ADR Regulations, but the current (2024) version defines serious ADRs in its Article 2, so the cross-reference is outdated. The clock runs from the day of awareness. Added a data element and a system. Double-check: quote lacks the lead-in "In any of the following situations," (cannot be added within the 1000-character limit); the cross-reference to Article 4 of the serious ADR Regulations is outdated against the 2024 text; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Implement risk management measures demanded by the authority
f.statement: When a drug is found with one of the Article 6(1) conditions, the central competent health authority may demand that the pharmaceutical dealer carry out risk management measures: release warnings or equivalents; revise the package insert; submit a Drug Safety Report; suspend use and sale; recall the product; or other necessary measures. Once demanded, the pharmaceutical dealer shall implement the measures.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.exceptions: Applies only when the authority makes the demand (authority discretion: 'may').
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Safety labeling; Safety communications

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical dealer (permit holder), when demanded by the central competent health authority
rows.quote:
When drugs are found with one of the conditions under respective sub-paragraphs of Paragraph 1 in the preceding article, the central competent health authority may demand that the pharmaceutical dealer enforces the risk management below:
1. Release warnings or their equivalents.
2. Revise the package insert.
3. Submit the Drug Safety Report.
4. Suspend the use and sale.
5. Recall the product.
6. Other necessary measures.
rows.review_note: Review: level Permitted -> Mandatory. The 'may' is the authority's discretion to demand; the dealer's duty is to comply once demanded (consistent with PAA Article 48 treatment). Statement and actor restated as a conditional duty. Double-check: Mandatory accepted as a judgement call: statement is framed as the dealer duty to implement measures once demanded, but the quote only gives the authority power to demand them and states no sanction; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Submit periodic drug safety update reports for five years and a summary report at permit expiry
f.statement: For new drugs under Article 7 of the Act, the pharmaceutical dealer shall submit the Periodic Drug Safety Update Report (Appendix 1) to the central competent health authority within five years following issuance of the Drug Permit, and the Drug Safety Summary Report (Appendix 2) upon expiration of the Permit. The data lock point is every six months for the first and second years after issuance and once a year for the remaining three years.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). New drugs under Article 7 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.deadline: DLP every 6 months in years 1-2 after permit issuance, yearly in years 3-5; summary report upon permit expiry
rows.quote:
The pharmaceutical dealer shall submit the Periodic Drug Safety Update Report (See Appendix 1) to the central competent health authority within five years following the issuance of the Drug Permit for new drugs under Article 7 of the Act by the said authority and the Drug Safety Summary Report (See Appendix 2) upon expiration of the said Permit.
The data lock point (DLP) for the periodic report in the preceding paragraph shall be once every six months for the first and the second years following issuance of the Permit and once every year for the remaining three years.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the PSUR and summary report duty and the DLP schedule; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Option to apply for DLP re-calculation based on IBD within 3 months
f.statement: Within three months from the day after receipt of the notification to pick up the Drug Permit, the pharmaceutical dealer may apply to the central competent health authority for re-calculation of the DLP, enclosing the international birth date (IBD) or the PSUR start date approved by an A10 country, and the planned DLPs for each term; the interval between terms shall not exceed one year.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). New drugs under Article 7 of the Act. Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.exceptions: Interval between reporting terms must not exceed one year.

rows.deadline: Within 3 months from the day after receipt of the notification to pick up the Permit
rows.quote:
The pharmaceutical dealer may enclose the following materials within three months from the next date upon receipt of the notification for picking up the Permit indicated in Paragraph 1 and apply with the central competent health authority for re-calculation of the DLP:
1. The international birth date (IBD) or the start date of the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) approved by one of the A10 countries.
2. The planning of the DLP for the collection of data for the reports respective term reports. The interval between terms, however, shall not exceed one year.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Permitted level matches "may"; the one-year maximum interval is a condition of the option; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Submit periodic and summary reports within 90 days of the DLP
f.statement: The periodic and summary reports under Article 8(1) shall be submitted within 90 days of the expiration of the DLP for the data of the respective term.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). New drugs under Article 7 of the Act. Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.quote: The periodic and summary reports indicated in Paragraph 1 shall be submitted within 90 days of the expiration of the DLP for data of the respective terms.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive provision, actor inferred from Article 8(1); clock runs from expiry of the DLP; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Continue collecting data and reporting for a designated period when demanded
f.statement: After receiving the summary report, the central competent health authority may, when it considers it necessary, demand that the pharmaceutical dealer continue to collect data and submit reports as in Article 8 for a designated period, and may do so more than once. Once demanded, the dealer shall continue collection and reporting for the designated period.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.exceptions: Applies only when the authority makes the demand (authority discretion: 'may').

rows.actor: Pharmaceutical dealer (permit holder), when demanded by the central competent health authority
rows.quote: Upon receipt of the summary report indicated in Paragraph 1 of the preceding article, when it is considered necessary, the central competent health authority may demand that the pharmaceutical dealer continue to collect the data and submit the report as indicated in the preceding article for a designated period; such designation is not limited to once.
rows.review_note: Review: level Permitted -> Mandatory. The authority has discretion to demand ('may'); the dealer must comply once demanded. Statement restated accordingly. Double-check: Mandatory accepted as a judgement call: statement is framed as the dealer duty to continue collection and reporting once demanded, but the quote only gives the authority power to demand and states no sanction; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Prepare a Risk Assessment and Control Plan within 3 months when announced and obtain approval before enforcing
f.statement: The central competent health authority may announce or approve drugs of a specific type or composition and demand that the pharmaceutical dealer prepare a Risk Assessment and Control Plan (Appendix 3). When so demanded, the dealer shall prepare the plan within three months following the date of announcement or approval and submit it to the authority for approval before it may be enforced. The plan shall cover the methods of risk assessment and control, the deadline for submitting the report, and other matters to be implemented.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Drugs of a specific type or composition announced or approved by the authority. Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.exceptions: Applies only to drugs of a specific type or composition announced or approved by the authority under Article 10(1).

rows.deadline: Within 3 months following the date of announcement or approval
rows.quote:
The central competent health authority may announce or approve drugs of a specific type or composition and demand that the pharmaceutical dealer prepares the Risk Assessment and Control Plan (See Appendix 3) within three months following the date of announcement of approval and submit it to the central competent health authority for approval before it may be enforced.
The Plan in the preceding paragraph shall cover the methods of risk assessment and control, the deadline for submitting the report, and other matters to be implemented.
rows.review_note: Review: statement made explicitly conditional on the authority's demand; otherwise no change. Double-check: duty arises only on the authority demand; the source reads "date of announcement of approval" (likely "or"), so the clock start is slightly uncertain; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Obtain approval before enforcing changes to the Risk Assessment and Control Plan
f.statement: Changes to the Risk Assessment and Control Plan shall be submitted to and approved by the central competent health authority before they may be enforced, except changes to the name, address, correspondence site, telephone or fax number of the pharmaceutical dealer or manufacturer, or the name or address of the distributor.
f.topic: Risk assessment and control plan changes
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.exceptions: Administrative changes (dealer/manufacturer name, address, contact details; distributor name or address) do not need prior approval.

rows.quote:
Changes to the Plan indicated in the preceding paragraph, if any, shall be submitted to and approved by the central competent health authority before they may be enforced, except for the following changes:
1. Name, address, correspondence site, telephone, or fax number of the pharmaceutical dealer or manufacturer.
2. Name or address of the distributor.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive provision, actor inferred; quote proves the prior-approval rule and exceptions; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Report completed portion within 60 days on business suspension or closure
f.statement: If periodic or summary reports under Articles 8 or 9 are not submitted, or the Risk Assessment and Control Plan is not completely enforced, because the pharmaceutical dealer suspends business operations or goes out of business, a report on the portion already completed shall be submitted within 60 days after the suspension or discontinuation. Implementation shall continue upon restored operation.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.processes: Aggregate reporting; Risk management & minimisation; Submission operations

rows.deadline: Within 60 days after suspension or discontinuation of operation
rows.quote: In the event that the periodic and summary reports of drug safety indicated in Article 8 or 9 are not submitted or the Risk Assessment and Control Plan in the preceding article is not completely enforced as a result of the pharmaceutical dealer suspends business operations or going out of business, a report shall be submitted on the portion that is already completed within 60 days after the occurrence of facts of suspended or discontinued operation. Implementation shall be continuing upon restored operation in the future.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive provision, actor inferred; 60-day clock from suspension or discontinuation proved; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Retain drug safety surveillance data for 5 years after permit expiry
f.statement: Drug safety surveillance-related data, including the source data, files, documents and publications needed to complete the plan or report, shall be retained by the pharmaceutical dealer for five years after the expiration of the drug permit.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.deadline: 5 years after expiration of the drug permit
rows.quote:
The drug safety surveillance-related data defined herein shall be retained by the pharmaceutical dealer for five years after the expiration of the drug permit.
The data indicated in the preceding paragraph include the source data, files, documents, and publications needed to complete the said plan or report.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor, retention period and data scope; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Hand over surveillance data on permit transfer; assignee continues surveillance
f.statement: Once transfer registration of a drug permit is approved, the assignor shall hand over drug safety surveillance-related data to the assignee, and the assignee shall continue the surveillance and store the data as required.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: Assignor and assignee of a transferred drug permit
rows.quote: Once transfer registration is approved by the central competent health authority for a drug permit, the assignor shall hand over drug safety surveillance-related data to the assignee and the assignee shall continue with the surveillance effort and store the data as required herein.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves both duties; RACI mapping to alliance safety lead is a judgement; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Do not evade, impede or refuse surveillance inspections or data requests
f.statement: The central competent health authority may send personnel to inspect the drug safety surveillance process or request relevant data; the pharmaceutical dealer shall not evade, impede or refuse such inspection or request.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.quote: The central competent health authority may send personnel to inspect the drug safety surveillance process or request the provision of relevant data. The pharmaceutical dealer shall not evade, impede or refuse such inspection or request.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the prohibition and actor; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Prepare plans and reports in Traditional Chinese or English
f.statement: Plans and reports under these Regulations shall be prepared in Traditional Chinese or English; appendixes in other languages require separate Traditional Chinese versions or English translations.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.quote: The plan and report defined herein shall be prepared in Traditional Chinese or English. When the appendixes are not in Traditional Chinese or English, their Traditional Chinese versions or English translations shall be prepared separately.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive provision, actor inferred; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.

f.title: Comply with the Personal Data Protection Act in safety surveillance
f.statement: When pharmaceutical dealers collect, process or use personal data to conduct drug safety surveillance, they shall follow the Personal Data Protection Act and related regulations.
f.applicability: Taiwan; official English translation from the Laws & Regulations Database (Chinese text prevails). Revised Regulations apply from 1 January 2023 (Article 16).

rows.quote: When the pharmaceutical dealers need to collect, process, or utilize personal data in order to conduct drug safety surveillance, they shall follow the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Act and its relevant regulations.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves actor and duty; English translation, so held below 90 per GUIDE.
